prompt: What does a component receive as `children`?

choices.text: The components it imports in its own script
choices.why: Imports are its own; `children` comes from whoever uses it.

choices.text: The content written between its opening and closing tags
choices.why: Right, as a snippet it renders with `{@render children()}`.

choices.text: Every element nested anywhere under it in the final page, as a list of DOM nodes
choices.why: It is markup to render, not a list of nodes to inspect.

choices.text: The props the parent passed, collected in an array
choices.why: That is closer to `...rest`.

prompt: After the change, `look` shows `region "Spanish"`. What gives the region that name?
hint: Two attributes point at each other.

choices.text: The `title` prop, which Svelte copies onto the section as an attribute
choices.why: Svelte copies nothing on its own; the panel's markup does the naming.

choices.text: `aria-labelledby` pointing at the heading's `id`
choices.why: Right. The section is named by its own heading.

choices.text: The `<style>` block's border, which marks it as a box
choices.why: A screen reader never sees the border.

choices.text: The course's id from the data file
choices.why: The id is `spanish`; the name shown is the heading's text.

prompt: Why does `Panel` use `$props.id()` rather than a fixed id such as `"panel-title"`?
hint: Think of two panels on one page.

choices.text: Each panel needs its own id, the same on the server and in the browser
choices.why: Right. A fixed id would repeat, and `aria-labelledby` would point at the wrong heading.

choices.text: Fixed ids are forbidden inside components
choices.why: They are allowed; they just repeat when the component is used twice.

choices.text: `$props.id()` makes the heading focusable
choices.why: It produces a string and nothing else.

prompt: The `.done` rule is in the page's `<style>`, and the label is rendered inside `Panel`. Why does the line-through still appear?

choices.text: Scoped styles leak into child components by default
choices.why: They do not leak; the label is the page's own markup.

choices.text: `Panel` copies its parent's styles
choices.why: `Panel` knows nothing about the page's styles.

choices.text: The label is the page's markup, so it carries the page's scoping class
choices.why: Right. Content passed as children belongs to the component that wrote it.

choices.text: `.done` is a global class built into Svelte
choices.why: It is a class the page defined.

prompt: A snippet is declared with `{#snippet name(…)}` and drawn with `{@___ name(…)}`.
Inside the page's `sessionLine` snippet, why can it call `format` without receiving it as a parameter?

choices.text: Svelte passes every import into every snippet automatically
choices.why: Nothing is passed; the snippet reads its surroundings.

choices.text: It reads what is in scope where it was declared
choices.why: Right, as a nested function reads the variables around it.

choices.text: `format` is a global function in every component that the browser provides to scripts
choices.why: It comes from `week.js`, imported by the page.

prompt: A snippet is declared inside an `{#each}` block. Where can it be rendered?
hint: Compare a variable declared in a block.

choices.text: Anywhere in the component, and in its `<script>`
choices.why: That holds for a top-level snippet.

choices.text: In any component that imports this one, under the snippet's name
choices.why: Snippets are not exported that way.

choices.text: Only inside that block, like a variable declared there
choices.why: Right, as a variable declared in a block is visible only there.

choices.text: Nowhere: snippets cannot be declared inside blocks
choices.why: They can; their visibility is just narrower.

prompt: The snippet's checkbox is bound to `session.done`. Why is that allowed when the snippet is rendered by another component?

choices.text: The snippet belongs to the page, which owns the session
choices.why: Right. Where it is rendered does not change who wrote it.

choices.text: Bindings inside snippets are ignored, so nothing is changed
choices.why: Ticking the box does change `done`.

choices.text: The rendering component automatically declares `session` with `$bindable` on its side
choices.why: Nothing is declared for you; ownership is the reason.

prompt: The page declares `{#snippet row(session)}` between `<List>` and `</List>`. What does `List` receive?

choices.text: A `children` snippet that contains the row
choices.why: A named snippet between the tags becomes a prop with its own name.

choices.text: A prop named `row`, holding the snippet itself
choices.why: Right, as if the page had written `row={row}`.

choices.text: An array of rendered `<li>` elements, one for every session of the selected course
choices.why: It receives the snippet and renders it itself.

choices.text: Nothing, until it declares a `<slot name="row">`
choices.why: Slots are Svelte 4; snippets need no slot.

choices.text: After `Next week`, in the week of 26 October

choices.text: After ticking every session done

choices.text: When Guitar was selected

prompt: You want the sessions shown as a table rather than a list. Which file changes?

choices.text: `+page.svelte`, since it declares the row
choices.why: The row is content; the `<ul>` around it is `List`'s.

choices.text: Both, in step, because each one depends on the other's markup
choices.why: They depend only on the snippet's name and parameter.

choices.text: `List.svelte`, since the structure is its own
choices.why: Right. The structure is `List`'s.

choices.text: `Panel.svelte`, which wraps the list
choices.why: `Panel` renders its children and knows nothing of lists.

prompt: What does a snippet compile to?

choices.text: A function
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A string of HTML stored once in the template
choices.why: Templates hold static markup; a snippet is called with arguments.

choices.text: A separate component file
choices.why: It stays inside the component that declared it.

choices.text: A custom element registered with the browser
choices.why: Nothing is registered with the browser.

prompt: In `$.snippet(node_1, () => $$props.row, () => $.get(item))`, why is the argument wrapped in a function?

choices.text: To delay rendering until the browser is idle
choices.why: It renders right away; the function is about reading.

choices.text: So each use reads `item` live, and a row updates when it changes
choices.why: Right. A parameter is a way of reading, not a copy.

choices.text: Because the compiler cannot pass objects to functions
choices.why: It could; it chooses not to copy.

prompt: What does `$$props.empty ?? $.noop` do when the page passes no `empty` snippet?

choices.text: Throws an error naming the missing snippet
choices.why: `?.()` asked for the opposite.

choices.text: Renders the `row` snippet instead, with no item
choices.why: Nothing substitutes `row` for `empty`.

choices.text: Renders nothing, through a function that does nothing
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Waits for the page to pass one later before showing the list at all
choices.why: The list renders as usual; only the empty branch is blank.

prompt: Match each framework with how it passes markup that uses the component's data.
How does React's render prop differ from a Svelte snippet?

choices.text: A render prop cannot receive data from the child that calls it with each item
choices.why: It receives the item, as a snippet does.

choices.text: A render prop must be named `children`
choices.why: Any prop name works.

choices.text: React calls it again on every single render of the parent
choices.why: Right. A snippet is set up once, with live parameters.

prompt: In Svelte 4, what did `let:item={session}` on a slotted element do?
hint: Data coming back into the slot.

choices.text: Received `item` from the slot, named `session`
choices.why: Right, the job a snippet parameter does now.

choices.text: Declared a new reactive variable called `item` in the page's script, holding the session
choices.why: It named the slot's data inside that element only.

choices.text: Bound the session two ways to the child
choices.why: That is `bind:`, not `let:`.

choices.text: Marked the element as optional
choices.why: It was about data, not optionality.

prompt: Which limits of Svelte 4 slots do snippets remove? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Needing a wrapper for named content of two elements
choices.why: Yes: `<svelte:fragment>`.

choices.text: Not being able to pass one on as a value
choices.why: Yes: a snippet is a value.

choices.text: Content being rendered on the server
choices.why: Both render on the server.

choices.text: Needing a special directive, `let:`, to receive data
choices.why: Yes: parameters replace it.

hint: The page hands over first; the checkbox appears last.
trap: `List` cannot render a snippet it has not yet received.

prompt: A `Dialog` component should hold any form a page puts in it. Which design fits?

choices.text: A prop for each kind of form the dialog might hold
choices.why: That makes the dialog know its contents.

choices.text: Render `children` where the content goes
choices.why: Right: it works for anything, and the form stays the page's.

choices.text: Import every form into the dialog and pick one by a `type` prop the page passes in
choices.why: Each new form would mean editing the dialog.

prompt: `Panel` is used with nothing between its tags and renders `{@render children()}`. What change lets it show just its heading?

choices.text: Give `children` a default of an empty string in `$props()`
choices.why: A string is not a snippet, and cannot be rendered.

choices.text: Write `{@render children?.()}`
choices.why: Right: nothing is rendered when there are no children.

choices.text: Wrap the render tag in `{#key children}`
choices.why: A key block recreates content; it does not make it optional.

choices.text: Nothing: Svelte skips a missing snippet by itself
choices.why: Calling a missing snippet fails; `?.()` is what skips it.

prompt: The page replaces its `row` snippet with another while the list is on screen. What does `List` render?
hint: Look at the first argument of `$.snippet`.

choices.text: The first `row` it received, kept until the list is created again
choices.why: It asks for `$$props.row` each time rather than keeping it.

choices.text: The new snippet
choices.why: Right, because the snippet is read through a function.

choices.text: Both, one after the other in each row
choices.why: Only the current `row` is rendered.

choices.text: An error, since props cannot change after mount
choices.why: Props change all the time; that is how they stay reactive.
